why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 only asks for the upper-cased greeting. Exact `HELLO, ADA!\n`, exit 0 and the flag-after-name case are under Advisory. Check 2 compares head output to the merge base without --shout, which is what "unchanged" means. Check 3 asks that docs/index.md mention --shout and say what it does, which "documents" requires. Check 4 can't fetch the live page before merge, so it checks the source of that page: the workflow still publishes docs/ on push to main, and docs/index.md lists --shout. It also reports that the live result waits for merge. This is a borderline call: a PR that moved publishing to another folder that also lists --shout would fail check 4 even though the expect line could still hold. I treat it as a stand-in for "after merge … lists --shout" rather than an extra rule. Usage exit 2, `npm test` passing and test coverage are all under Advisory. No PASS or FAIL condition requires exact wording, a mutation test, or a branch or file-scope rule.
